newsitem.title: USA: O&R, Central Hudson settlement changes urged.
newsitem.headline: O&R, Central Hudson settlement changes urged.

text.p: Changes are needed in the restructuring settlements Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc and Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp reached with the staff of the New York State Public Service Commission, according to the commission administrative law judges that reviewed the agreements.
A third law judge found the overall settlement Rochester Gas and Electric Corp reached with the staff was reasonable, noting it was clear the company "made substantial concessions."

Timothy Carey, chairman of the New York State Consumer Protection Board called the judge's recommendation "a bad, bad decision," that will do little to help lower Rochester Gas & Electric's electric rates.
The settlement is "anti-compeititve," he said, adding "it allows RG&E to earn excess profits over its cost of equity of 10.2 percent."
The judge that reviewed the Orange & Rockland seettlement recommended that the commission "not endorse the agreement as submitted. Rather, it should be redurned to the parties for modification."
The judge in the Central Hudson case said "the settlement raises serious problems under every element of the Guidelines" set by the commission for restructuring the state's electric power industry.

"There is little bvasis for confidence in the settlement as a resonable proxy for a litigated outcome," the decision continued, pointing out "the only agreement (for most of the normally adversarial parties in this case) is that they cannot support the settlement."

In June, a law judge said Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's settlement with the commission needs further negotiation. The record was closed on that case Friday with the filing of briefs opposing exceptions to the law judge's views, which had been filed on July 10.
